title: Stan Wawrinka Says Goodbye After a 23-Year Tennis Career
summary:
Stan Wawrinka has always known how to stir a crowd, and that did not change in the final tour-level match of his career. The 41-year-old Swiss star lost to Czech opponent Jiri Lehecka in front of passionate home support in Basel on Tuesday, but he left showing the hallmarks of a career that exceeded expectations.

There was the stylish one-handed backhand down the line, the finger pointing to his temple, and the demand for more noise from the stands. There was the roar of "Allez!" after winning a point he probably should not have won. And there were tears, too, as Wawrinka, his family, and his team took in the reality of an honourable 7-5, 7-6 (7-2) defeat.

The loss brought an end to a professional career spanning 23 years, 985 matches, and three Grand Slam titles. Wawrinka, a former world number three, told the ATP website that all he wanted was to give everything, have no regrets, and always fight and give 100 percent in every match, out of respect for himself, his opponent, the tournament, and the fans.

So many talented players of his generation felt that Roger Federer, Rafael Nadal, and Novak Djokovic, known as the 'Big Three,' were a blockade preventing them from becoming a Grand Slam champion. It did not stop Wawrinka. With explosive shot-making and relentless endurance, he barrelled past the trio on his way to winning his three major titles.

His career had been ticking along steadily until he lifted one of the sport's biggest prizes at the age of 28. At the 2015 French Open, he beat Federer in the quarter-finals, then beat Djokovic in the final.
why_it_matters: Wawrinka's farewell shows that persistence and full effort can carry a player past even the strongest rivals, and that a long career can be honoured even in defeat.
